shared.title: The shared cells
shared.summary: The cells both quickstarts are built with: connection, a loader for each source, and a role review that profiles and approves the selected table. Open your persona's quickstart instead.

notebooks.title: Start here: access and understand your data
notebooks.summary: Steps 1 and 2 of the journey, plus a step 0: check, update or extend the kit from the notebook itself (nb.kit_check, nb.exakit), with the log shown in the cell. Opens connected; load a sample, your own CSV, Parquet or JSON file, or a connected source; review the proposed column roles (the guesses first) and approve them before the first query. Ends by opening 01_explore.

notebooks.title: Prepare, explore, model, validate
notebooks.summary: Steps 3 to 6: check the data is clean (repeats, gaps, placeholders, a rare label), see the schema's links and a joined view, a typed and cleaned view; compare groups and follow the label over time with the SQL visible; leave out a column that gives the label away, train a small scikit-learn model on this computer from the category, entity and month (no date needed), then validate it on the rows it never saw and read what it leans on. With a text column, a text step with your own model, traced to Langfuse.
notebooks.needs: a loaded dataset; a model for the optional AI step

notebooks.title: Ask your data with AI
notebooks.summary: Step 7: ask in plain English; the starter SQL or your own AI model (external or local) drafts the query from the approved column map only - no rows are sent - traced to Langfuse when set up; inspect and edit it, then explicitly approve the exact query before it runs with the read-only database identity.
notebooks.needs: an approved dataset; optionally a model to draft SQL

notebooks.title: Share the insight and hand it off
notebooks.summary: Steps 8 and 9: install and start Dash Server from the notebook, prepare a dashboard from approved roles and visible SQL, inspect its preview, promote only after checking the figures; then pack the approved column map, every query with its digest, the dashboards and the workflow log into one hand-off folder and zip (nb.handoff_bundle).
notebooks.needs: an approved dataset; Dash Server is installed and started from the notebook

notebooks.title: Quickstart
notebooks.summary: Opens connected. Checks the container, MLflow server and bucket directory; loads data, then lets you review and approve proposed column roles. Ends by opening 01_train.

notebooks.title: Train inside the database
notebooks.summary: Writes or checks the training handoff from the approved column map, builds its SQL feature view, trains a logistic regression on the 0/1 target (amazon_sales: CANCELLED; walmart_sales: ABOVE_STORE_MEDIAN) inside a Python UDF, and logs metrics, baseline, model and coefficients to MLflow.
notebooks.needs: an approved column map with a target, udf-devkit, MLflow

notebooks.title: Score with Rust
notebooks.summary: Build a Rust UDF from 01_train's coefficients and compare its predictions with Python on the same test rows.
notebooks.needs: a 01_train run, the Rust container, Docker or Podman

notebooks.title: Score a model trained elsewhere
notebooks.summary: Brings a model trained anywhere into the bucket directory with exakit model put, creates the scoring UDF from the template, scores a table and compares with the prediction on this computer.
